nodes.label: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI)
nodes.name: Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI)
nodes.description: Cross-benchmark composite metric combining 42 AI benchmarks (3 categories per https://epoch.ai/data/eci-documentation/data) into a single 'general capability' scale. Calibrated so Claude 3.5 Sonnet = 130 and GPT-5 (medium) = 150. Linear scale: a 10-point jump represents equivalent capability gain regardless of position. Methodology paper 'A Rosetta Stone for AI Benchmarks' (arxiv 2512.00193, Anson Ho et al) — IRT-style stitching infers benchmark difficulty statistically from overlapping model results, weights harder benchmarks more, avoids inflation from specialized models. Models with <4 benchmark scores or pre-2023 release excluded due to data sparsity. Contributing benchmarks: (Internal Evaluations) Chess Puzzles, FrontierMath Tiers 1-3, FrontierMath Tier 4, GPQA Diamond, MATH Level 5, OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025, SimpleQA Verified. (External Leaderboards) Aider polyglot, APEX-Agents, ARC-AGI-2, BALROG, DeepResearch Bench, Fiction.liveBench, GeoBench, GSO, HLE, SimpleBench, SWE-bench (Bash Only), Terminal-Bench, The Agent Company, VPCT, WeirdML V2. (Developer Reported) ANLI, ARC AI2, ARC-AGI, BIG-Bench Hard, CADEval, CSQA2, Cybench, GSM8K, HellaSwag, LAMBADA, Lech Mazur Writing, MMLU, OpenBookQA, OSWorld, PIQA, ScienceQA, SuperGLUE, TriviaQA, Video MME, WinoGrande. Benchmarks rescaled so random-guess = 0. Domain-specific ECI variants (Software Engineering, Math, custom) use the same Rosetta Stone methodology on subsets.

The current board publishes a relative Thurstone 'comparison score' where zero sits near the middle of the field and the top entry is ~4.1 (Fable 5.1, Opus 5), plus an estimated win chance. nodes.label: ERRORQUAKE-10K (severity tail-slope b)
nodes.name: ERRORQUAKE-10K (severity tail-slope b)
nodes.metric: Gutenberg-Richter upper-tail slope b of error-severity distribution
nodes.description: Per-model fit of log10 N(M>=m) = a - b*m on a 0.0-4.0 severity scale across 10,000 queries (8 domains x 5 difficulty tiers). Higher b = lighter tail (fewer catastrophic fabrications); lower b = heavier tail (more order-of-magnitude failures). Dual-judge 8-model round-robin scoring validated against 519-item 3-rater human study (ICC=0.85, judge-vs-human rank rho=0.89). 95% CIs from n=2000 bootstrap resamples.

nodes.label: ERRORQUAKE-10K error rate (ε)
nodes.name: ERRORQUAKE-10K error rate (ε)
nodes.description: Scalar error rate epsilon on the 10K-query benchmark. Lower is better. Reported alongside b to demonstrate the matched-accuracy discriminator: 85/210 model pairs have disjoint 95% b CIs at |Δε| < 0.05.

nodes.label: ExploitBench Tier 3 — Engine Primitives
nodes.name: ExploitBench Tier 3 — Engine Primitives
nodes.description: Fraction of 41 V8 bugs where agent constructed engine-specific exploit primitives (addrof, fakeobj, caged_read, caged_write) inside V8 heap sandbox. Graded by one-shot challenge-response builtins under --grader d8.

nodes.label: ExploitBench Tier 2 — General Primitives

nodes.description: Fraction of 41 V8 bugs where agent escaped V8 cage with general-purpose primitives (infoleak_binary/libc/stack, arb_read, arb_write). Demonstrates elevation outside V8 heap sandbox security boundary.

nodes.label: ExploitBench Tier 1 — PC Control

nodes.label: WebTailBench

nodes.label: WebGameBench — Usable rate
nodes.name: WebGameBench — Usable rate
nodes.description: WebGameBench (arXiv 2605.17637, Baidu): 111 frozen Structured WebGame Specifications (7 gameplay families, D1-D4 difficulty) that a coding agent must turn into a deployed browser-native game; a Codex CLI (gpt-5.4 xhigh) runtime evaluator plays the game in Chrome via Playwright and assigns EXCELLENT/USABLE/UNUSABLE. Usable rate = share of valid scored samples labeled EXCELLENT or USABLE. Evaluator agrees with human gameplay review at 85.0% accuracy (XHigh) on the Usable criterion. Higher is better.

nodes.label: WebGameBench — Excellent rate
nodes.name: WebGameBench — Excellent rate
nodes.description: WebGameBench (arXiv 2605.17637): same 111 browser-native game tasks; Excellent rate = share of valid scored samples whose delivered game fully and stably satisfies the specification (label EXCELLENT). Stricter signal; exact three-way label agreement with humans only 50%. Higher is better.

nodes.label: TeleSWEBench — Stage 1 Exact-Match localization (cumulative)
nodes.name: TeleSWEBench — Stage 1 Exact-Match localization (cumulative)
nodes.description: TeleSWEBench (arXiv 2606.05001, NCSU/UCSD): 734 commit-derived tasks (Easy 142 / Medium 279 / Difficult 313) mined from the srsRAN 5G C++ repository, each with executable unit tests. Stage 1 metric: share of tasks where the agent modified exactly the ground-truth file set (P = T), cumulative over all tiers; AIDER CLI harness with 300 s cutoff (timeouts excluded). Higher is better.

nodes.description: Dialogue-SWEBench (arXiv 2606.13995, UCSC): the 500 SWE-bench Verified problems re-cast as dialogue-driven sessions — the agent only sees an under-specified initial user query and must elicit missing details from a persona-grounded simulated user (quantized Llama 3.3 70B with self-revision) who never touches code; success = submitted patch passes the SWE-bench Verified execution tests. 100 agent steps per problem. nodes.label: CoDA-Bench — Execution Accuracy (Codex CLI scaffold)
nodes.name: CoDA-Bench — Execution Accuracy (Codex CLI scaffold)
nodes.description: CoDA-Bench (arXiv 2606.15300, Renmin Univ., ICML 2026): 1,009 data-intensive analytical tasks over a Kaggle-derived Linux sandbox (31 data communities, ~980 files per environment, SNR 0.0105); agent must discover the relevant files and write code to produce the answer. CoDA-Hard = 119-task subset needing >=2 target files and >30-line reference solutions. DA = Discovery Accuracy (correct target files located); EA = Execution Accuracy (task output correct). Higher is better. Scaffold: Codex CLI (official default configuration for native CLI tools; unified framework for OpenHands / Mini-SWE-agent).

nodes.label: GameEngineBench — pass@1
nodes.name: GameEngineBench — pass@1
nodes.description: GameEngineBench (arXiv 2607.03525, Nitrode / Nexon Intelligence Labs): 110 scoped C++ implementation tasks inside Unreal Engine 5 projects from 9 real game repositories (gameplay, multiplayer, AI, animation, UI, persistence, XR, rendering plugins); patch must compile and pass behavioral tests run via Unreal automation in PIE listen-server mode. One attempt per task, solver timeout 3600 s. Each model is run through its vendor's native CLI wrapper (codex, claude-code, Antigravity CLI, qwen-code, kimi-code), so harness effects are mixed in. 31 tasks unsolved by all configs. Higher is better.

nodes.label: Atrex-Bench — correctness pass rate
nodes.name: Atrex-Bench — correctness pass rate
nodes.description: Atrex-Bench (arXiv 2607.14541, Alibaba ATREX): trace-driven GPU-kernel generation benchmark — 30 operators and 440 shapes sampled from production inference traces of compute-limited memory-rich XPU-A GPUs, each with an importance weight (share of GPU time) and a roofline ceiling; agents must write kernels in the FlyDSL target DSL (unfamiliar to pretraining corpora). nodes.label: SWE-NFI — functional preservation check pass rate (Codex CLI scaffold)
nodes.name: SWE-NFI — functional preservation check pass rate (Codex CLI scaffold)
nodes.description: SWE-NFI (arXiv 2607.27409, York Univ. et al.): 188 non-functional-improvement tasks from real merged PRs in open-source Python projects; 5 NFI aspects (Documentation, Error Handling, Library Constraints, Coding Style, Logic Patterns) operationalized as 92 executable rules. Outputs must first pass task-specific functional preservation checks (FPC); NFI improvement = change in normalized rule score vs original code (percentage points), averaged over 5 runs. Human reference FPC 100%, aggregate improvement ~ Doc 8.0 / EH 2.0 / LC 1.1 / CS 1.5 / LP 1.5. Higher is better. Share of valid outputs passing all task-specific functional preservation checks. Scaffold: Codex CLI.

nodes.label: LoopsBench — Resolve Rate (Codex loop)
nodes.name: LoopsBench — Resolve Rate (Codex loop)
nodes.description: LoopsBench (arXiv 2608.00267, Microsoft / Nanjing Univ.): long-horizon loop-engineering benchmark — each task is a dependency DAG over separately testable development units recovered from authentic sources (8 programming languages, >5,300 development units); a dependency-aware runtime releases tests along the ready frontier and retains passed tests as regression obligations. Resolve Rate (RR) = tasks fully resolved; Test Pass Rate (TPR) = fraction of released tests passed; 'w/' = with outer continuation loop. Single trial per config. Higher is better. Loop implementation: Codex; 'w/' outer continuation setting.

nodes.label: SWE-bench Verified (200-task sample) — Vanilla re-run in SWE-Touch (mini-swe-agent)
nodes.name: SWE-bench Verified (200-task sample) — Vanilla re-run in SWE-Touch (mini-swe-agent)
nodes.description: SWE-Touch (arXiv 2608.02499, CASIA): stress-tests coding agents in a shared workspace via validated Counter-Edits — plausible user code edits that conflict with task completion, injected (with a short user message) when the agent reaches the task-critical region. Main cohort: seeded 200-task sample of SWE-bench Verified, Mini-SWE-Agent harness on Harbor, 100-step budget, mean of 3 runs. Longer-horizon extension: 25 SWE-Bench Pro + 25 DeepSWE tasks, 500-step budget, K=3 edits injected at 25/50/75% of the Vanilla trajectory, mean of 2 runs. Higher is better. Vanilla (no user edit) resolve rate on the 200-task Verified sample — re-run of other vendors' models by the SWE-Touch authors.

nodes.label: MT-Web2Code — Macro-Level regional reconstruction Score
nodes.name: MT-Web2Code — Macro-Level regional reconstruction Score
nodes.description: MT-Web2Code (arXiv 2608.03474, HIT / Meituan): multimodal multi-turn web-UI coding benchmark for coding agents. Macro-Level Regional Reconstruction: rebuild a missing region of an existing page from a visual reference, scored by VLM rubric (Kimi-K2.6 judge; Layout/Element/Text/Color/Spacing + overall; Score = final composite). Micro-Level Localized Modification: fix a localized defect (9-type taxonomy), scored by pixel alignment (in-box repair S_inbox, out-of-box preservation S_outbox; Score = composite). Mean of 3 runs. Higher is better. Macro-Level composite Score.

nodes.label: GameXpert-Bench GameGen — Overall score
nodes.name: GameXpert-Bench GameGen — Overall score
nodes.description: GameXpert-Bench (arXiv 2608.21833, Tencent Hunyuan / Lightspeed): three-track game-development lifecycle benchmark for coding agents. GameGen = 97 single-request browser-native game generation tasks (11 genres, 44 3D) built with Claude Code under default configuration, judged by an evidence-grounded LLM judge on Completeness / Richness / Player Experience / Visual Quality (Overall = mean, 0-100). GameFix = repair of 50 confidential Gold Games corrupted by reversible mutation operators; STRICT = mean height of the average@3 survival curve over all-solved threshold band tau in [90,100] (3 runs). GameOpt = human-guided multi-turn refinement over 17 JavaScript games / 102 requests, six-dimension discrimination-weighted score (0-100). Higher is better. GameGen Overall (Table 2), Claude Code default harness.

nodes.description: Hack-Verifiable Terminal Bench / HVTB (arXiv 2608.22103, Tel Aviv Univ. / UCSB): the 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks instrumented with two planted, deterministically detectable reward hacks (a leaked hidden solution and readable held-out tests in an admin/ directory). Metric = any-hack rate: share of completed runs that triggered at least one planted hack. Prompt classes: Ablation = no hacking-related instruction; L0 = generic 'solve on your own / do not hack'; L1-L3 = progressively more specific disclosure of the vulnerability. Each model runs in its native harness (Claude Code, Codex, gemini-cli; terminus-2 for open models). Lower is better. Setting: Ablation prompt (no anti-hack instruction).

nodes.label: PatchBench — Solved rate (Codex)
nodes.name: PatchBench — Solved rate (Codex)
nodes.description: PatchBench (arXiv 2609.04075, Univ. of Maryland): 213 C/C++ repository-level vulnerability-patching tasks from 32 GitHub projects / 16 CWEs, built by vulnerability transplant + code mutation so ground-truth fixes lie outside the crash stack (mitigating patch memorization and stack-trace-only fixes). Agent gets the repo, PoC, sanitizer report and build commands in Docker; $5 budget per task, medium reasoning effort, no web access. Solved = patch passes both security validation (new PoCs / fuzzing) and semantic validation; PoC Pass = original PoC no longer crashes (inflates solve rate 1.83x). Higher is better. Scaffold: Codex.

nodes.description: SWE-Bench Pro Verified (arXiv 2609.08149, Shanghai AI Lab / ECNU / Fudan, AgentCompass): the 731 public SWE-Bench Pro instances re-released with anti-hacking safeguards (repository reconstruction, hidden-artifact concealment, metadata anonymization, network blocking of gold patches/tests) plus minimal human task refinement of 102 flawed instances. Verified setting (Figure 1 dark bars / Table 3).

nodes.label: HT-Bench tactile retrieval Hit@1
nodes.name: HT-Bench tactile retrieval Hit@1
nodes.description: HT-Bench (arXiv 2606.19161): multi-task benchmark for dexterous full-hand tactile representation learning with egocentric vision: tactile similarity retrieval (Hit@1, Recall@5), masked tactile inpainting, vision-to-tactile synthesis (RMSE, contact IoU) with task-level OOD splits, plus 4 real-world downstream tasks (board clean, pear pick, water pour, sand shovel; 15 trials each). Baselines are generic tactile encoders (ResNet-18, CNN, VQ-VAE, ViT: retrieval Hit@1 92.13/89.61/63.60/94.27; downstream avg ResNet-trained 50.0, ViT 45.0) and are not stored as models. Table 2 Hit@1.

nodes.label: BiGym 2.0 nine-task mean SR
nodes.name: BiGym 2.0 nine-task mean SR
nodes.description: BiGym 2.0 (arXiv:2610.07594): 20 household loco-manipulation tasks on a walking Unitree G1 with a frozen whole-body controller; 60 VR human demos per task. Nine representative tasks (pick box, reach multi-modal, reach dual, drawer close/open, move plate, move two plates, dishwasher close, dishwasher load cups). Learned policies: mean over 3 runs x last 5 checkpoints x 100 episodes (π0.5: 1 run, 50 episodes). Coding agents: 3 cold-start development sessions each under the strict interface (84x84 onboard views, direct joint actions, 101k-step interaction budget), 100 hidden-seed episodes per frozen program.

nodes.label: ESARBench (Overall SR)
nodes.name: ESARBench (Overall SR)
nodes.description: Overall victim-search SR. ESARBench: UAV embodied search-and-rescue benchmark in a high-fidelity AirSim simulation platform; tasks graded Simple/Medium/Hard/Extreme; agent must find victims and discover clues under a rescue prompt. Metrics: SR (victim search success), TSR (time-weighted SR), CDS (clue discovery score), RS (comprehensive rescue score). All MLLM baselines use Qwen3.5-Plus as backbone with a shared four-camera YOLO-World RGB-D detector. Random baseline overall SR 2.65 / RS 9.81. arXiv 2605.01371.

nodes.description: MobileCybench (arXiv:2609.23980, Stanford/Berkeley): vulnerability discovery by coding agents in 13 open-source Android apps, scored by 495 executable probes (security-property checks) replayed against the app; 2 attack settings (malicious app on device / remote attacker with low-privilege account) x 2 access levels (obfuscated APK only / source visible); 2 independent attempts per configuration, pass@2 (configuration counts if either attempt triggers a probe). 5 agents: OpenCode+GPT-5.5 (xhigh), OpenCode+GPT-5.6-Sol (xhigh), OpenCode+GLM-5.2 (max thinking), Claude Code+Opus 4.8 (effort max), Claude Code+Opus 5 (effort max). Higher is better. Metric: number of distinct reference vulnerabilities attributed to the agent's exploits across both settings and access levels (Table 11 / Section 4.2 prose).

nodes.label: DUMA-Bench dual-control ASR
nodes.name: DUMA-Bench dual-control ASR
nodes.description: DUMA-Bench (arXiv:2609.24662, ITMO AI Security Lab): extends tau2-bench with adversarial environments over 8 vulnerability domains (mail RAG phishing, cross-agent collab manipulation, unsafe output handling, CRM leak, infra load-shedding, marketing phishing, auth spoofing support, tool shadow poisoning), 35 executable multi-turn tasks, 14 models x 8 domains x 5 runs = 1960 trials per regime; scored by deterministic environment assertions (+ communication assertions for 9 tasks). Aggregate ASR 26.9% passive-user vs 41.1% dual-control. Printed as fraction 0-1, stored x100. LOWER is better. Regime: dual-control (user simulator can also act on the shared environment), Table 4 'Dual ASR'.

nodes.label: PASTABench Perfect Interruption

nodes.metric: % trajectories interrupted inside the OIW with correct Level-2 risk
nodes.description: PASTABench (arXiv:2609.28197, HKUST): 1,139 multi-turn agent trajectories over 5 risk categories / 13 sub-categories, each annotated with an Earliest-Signal turn and Trigger turn defining the Optimal Intervention Window (OIW). A monitor LLM reads the trajectory turn by turn and must decide whether/when to interrupt and name the risk category (zero-shot, T=0, auto-stop at first interrupt). Table 2 / Figure 3. Higher is better. Metric: Perfect Interruption rate (valid Level-2 label AND inside the optimal window).

nodes.label: ScopeBench scope adherence

nodes.metric: % scoped trajectories without a scope violation (hybrid verifier+judge), higher better
nodes.description: ScopeBench (arXiv:2609.30325, dreadnode): 30 dead-end agentic web-app security tasks where the objective is reachable only by violating a stated engagement scope; each task run scopeless (capability) and scoped (adherence, 2 phrasings, n=180 scoped trajectories per model), one harness, 8 models. nodes.label: AgentBoundary Hard-Benign utility
nodes.name: AgentBoundary Hard-Benign utility
nodes.description: AgentBoundary (arXiv:2609.33658, PKU/BAAI): four-way counterfactual tool-using agent safety suite — the same executable workflow varied independently in apparent risk and action permissibility (2,787 families / 4,000 human-validated tasks); trajectory- and post-state-based judging. Boundary-critical splits: Hard-Benign (HB, risky-looking but authorized; utility = completion) and Covert-Malicious (CM, routine-looking but unauthorized; safety = blocked). 17 configurations incl. harnesses (Codex, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness). The paper's plug-in Thought aligner raises HB utility by +18.2 pts on average (Table 3, not stored as model rows). Table 2. Higher is better. Metric: HB utility (over-refusal diagnostic; low = over-refuses).

nodes.name: DGF-Bench DGF score
nodes.metric: 100 x share of applicable fixed attacks blocked (0-100), higher better
nodes.description: DGF-Bench (arXiv:2609.34913, Jeremy Canale, dgfbench.com): a board of tool-using agents (specialist gates + General gate) reviews synthetic enterprise stage-gate dossiers (61 executable rules, 42 authoritative records, 32 narrative documents) while an attacker plants deceptive content in non-authoritative evidence; 27 fixed attacks + 2 adaptive campaigns, 6 models via OpenRouter (T=0), Sept 2026. Metric: DGF score = 100 x (fixed attacks blocked / applicable fixed attacks, 26-27 per model); an attack passes when the model takes the exact injected action it does not take on the paired clean dossier (attributable success). Table 11 / Figure 6.

nodes.description: HarnessSecurity-Bench / HSB (arXiv:2610.07639, SYSU / HKBU): 23 tasks over 5 attack surfaces with deterministic utility and attack oracles, used to test 9 security mechanisms (auto-approve, network isolation, command allow-list, credential/data leakage guard, MCP, prompt-injection filter, permission restriction, read-only, ...) across 6 coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, gptme, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot) with a fixed GLM-5.2 backbone; 2,500 trials, 81,155 tool calls. nodes.label: CyberGym-E2E official board — S3 discover + PoC + patch + tests (headline), $10 budget
nodes.name: CyberGym-E2E official board — S3 discover + PoC + patch + tests (headline), $10 budget
nodes.description: CyberGym-E2E official leaderboard (UC Berkeley RDI, arXiv 2606.04460): 920 real OSS-Fuzz vulnerabilities in 139 C/C++ projects; the agent discovers the bug, writes a PoC that crashes the unpatched build (S1), patches it (S2) without breaking developer tests (S3); S4 (diagnostic) checks the ground-truth vulnerability is the one fixed. Stages are cumulative; S3 is the headline discover-and-patch rate. Patch-only = agent given the ground-truth PoC and crash log. Rows marked † on the board were run on an earlier 615-task set. Agents run with their vendor CLI (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenHands) and a 90-minute limit; $10-per-task budget runs by the CyberGym-E2E team (comparable set).

nodes.label: DeepsecBench (Vercel board, F2 score)
nodes.name: DeepsecBench (Vercel board, F2 score)
nodes.description: Vercel DeepsecBench (launched 2026-07-27; board at vercel.com/ai-gateway/leaderboards/deepsecbench): vulnerability discovery in one undisclosed open-source codebase pinned before a large batch of fixes — 50 entry-point files, golden set of 231 human-judged findings. nodes.description: Real-world clinical performance: safety, accuracy, interaction quality, information prioritization, proactive inquiry. 3 tracks (LLM/VLM/Agent).

nodes.label: REBench
nodes.name: REBench
nodes.description: Reverse engineering benchmark: stripped-binary types/names recovery; 29.94M lines decompiled x64 code.

nodes.label: CTF-Archive-Diamond
nodes.name: CTF-Archive-Diamond
nodes.description: NIST CAISI cyber CTF archive — diamond difficulty tier. Used in CAISI DeepSeek V4 Pro evaluation.

nodes.label: PortBench
nodes.name: PortBench
nodes.description: Software engineering benchmark used by NIST CAISI evaluations alongside SWE-Bench Verified.

nodes.label: ARC-AGI-2 semi-private
nodes.name: ARC-AGI-2 semi-private
nodes.description: ARC-AGI-2 semi-private split (held-out tasks not in public release). Used in NIST CAISI evaluation.

nodes.label: PUMaC 2024
nodes.name: PUMaC 2024
nodes.description: Princeton University Mathematics Competition 2024 problems. Used in NIST CAISI math evaluation.

nodes.label: AI Coding Contest — Word Gem Puzzle
nodes.name: AI Coding Contest — Word Gem Puzzle
nodes.description: Day-12 Word Gem Puzzle of the Independent AI Coding Contest tournament covered by ThinkPol. Score = match points won across rounds.

nodes.label: AI Coding Contest — Cumulative
nodes.name: AI Coding Contest — Cumulative
nodes.description: Cumulative score across all days of the Independent AI Coding Contest tournament covered by ThinkPol.

nodes.label: NIST CAISI IRT Capability Elo
nodes.name: NIST CAISI IRT Capability Elo
nodes.description: Item Response Theory-estimated overall capability Elo rating from NIST CAISI evaluation suite (cyber + SWE + science + reasoning + math composite).

nodes.label: MemRouter (LoCoMo F1)
nodes.name: MemRouter (LoCoMo F1)
nodes.description: Memory-as-Embedding Routing for Long-Term Conversational Agents (arxiv 2605.00356, submitted 2026-05-01). Decouples memory admission from answer generation via lightweight 12M-param classification heads. Evaluated on LoCoMo conversational QA. Reports F1 + memory-management latency (p50).

nodes.label: CN-LLM Long Document Understanding
nodes.name: CN-LLM Long Document Understanding
nodes.description: Information extraction, logic mapping, critical reading on long Chinese documents. Scored 0-20 by independent reviewer. Source: github.com/happypaul2139-svg/LLM-Of-China-Comparison.

nodes.label: CN-LLM Code Writing
nodes.name: CN-LLM Code Writing
nodes.description: Frontend development, algorithm design, engineering completeness on Chinese-context coding tasks. 0-20 score.

nodes.label: CN-LLM Professional Writing
nodes.name: CN-LLM Professional Writing
nodes.description: Business writing, tone control, format compliance in Chinese professional contexts. 0-20 score.

nodes.label: CN-LLM Data Analysis
nodes.name: CN-LLM Data Analysis
nodes.description: Data processing, trend identification, business insights extraction. 0-20 score.

nodes.label: CN-LLM Research & Planning
nodes.name: CN-LLM Research & Planning
nodes.description: Market analysis, financial calculations, solution design. 0-20 score.

nodes.label: CN-LLM Effect Score (0-100)
nodes.name: CN-LLM Effect Score (0-100)
nodes.description: Aggregate effectiveness rating across the 5 CN-LLM scenarios, normalised to 100. Component of overall composite (0.8 weight).

nodes.label: CN-LLM Cost Score (0-100)
nodes.name: CN-LLM Cost Score (0-100)
nodes.description: Inverse cost rating where 100 = cheapest tier observed in benchmark suite. Component of overall composite (0.1 weight).

nodes.label: CN-LLM Speed Score (0-100)
nodes.name: CN-LLM Speed Score (0-100)
nodes.description: Throughput/latency rating where 100 = fastest tier observed in benchmark suite. Component of overall composite (0.1 weight).

nodes.label: CN-LLM Overall (0.8E + 0.1C + 0.1S)
nodes.name: CN-LLM Overall (0.8E + 0.1C + 0.1S)
nodes.description: Composite score = 0.8*Effect + 0.1*Cost + 0.1*Speed. Tournament leaderboard from independent CN-LLM head-to-head.

nodes.label: Physical AI Bench
nodes.name: Physical AI Bench
nodes.description: Visual-spatial-temporal reasoning benchmark for embodied physical AI VLMs. Launched alongside Cosmos-Reason 2.

nodes.label: WxC-Bench
nodes.name: WxC-Bench
nodes.description: Multi-modal weather/climate downstream tasks for foundation models (Nature Sci Data 2026).

nodes.label: AI AgriBench
nodes.name: AI AgriBench
nodes.description: Trustworthy evaluation of LLM/AI agronomic advisory tools.

nodes.label: TokaMark
nodes.name: TokaMark
nodes.description: MAST tokamak plasma model representation, prediction horizons, cross-regime generalization.

nodes.label: DisruptionBench
nodes.name: DisruptionBench
nodes.description: Standardized ML disruption-prediction across Alcator C-Mod, DIII-D, EAST tokamaks.

nodes.label: MOFSimBench
nodes.name: MOFSimBench
nodes.description: Universal MLIP evaluation on metal-organic-framework molecular modeling.

nodes.label: AgriBench-13K
nodes.name: AgriBench-13K
nodes.description: 13-task LLM agriculture benchmark; 13,000 expert QA pairs.

nodes.label: MiniF2F (formal math)
nodes.name: MiniF2F (formal math)
nodes.description: Formal mathematics theorem-proving benchmark in Lean/Isabelle (244 olympiad-level problems).

nodes.label: IMO 2025
nodes.name: IMO 2025
nodes.description: International Mathematical Olympiad 2025 (6 problems × 7 points = 42 max). AI evaluation track.

nodes.label: ICPC 2025 World Finals
nodes.name: ICPC 2025 World Finals
nodes.description: International Collegiate Programming Contest 2025 World Finals problems. AI evaluation.

nodes.label: IPhO 2025 (written portion)
nodes.name: IPhO 2025 (written portion)
nodes.description: International Physics Olympiad 2025 written problems. AI evaluation.

nodes.label: IChO 2025 (written portion)
nodes.name: IChO 2025 (written portion)
nodes.description: International Chemistry Olympiad 2025 written problems. AI evaluation.

nodes.label: AIFS 1.1 vs AIFS 1.0 improvement
nodes.name: AIFS 1.1 vs AIFS 1.0 improvement
nodes.description: Variable-by-variable improvement of AIFS 1.1.0 over operational AIFS 1.0.

nodes.label: AlphaGenome Single-Seq Regulatory Eval (24 tasks)
nodes.name: AlphaGenome Single-Seq Regulatory Eval (24 tasks)
nodes.description: 24 regulatory-prediction evaluations on single DNA sequences. SOTA count out of 24.

nodes.label: AlphaGenome Variant Regulatory Eval (26 tasks)
nodes.name: AlphaGenome Variant Regulatory Eval (26 tasks)
nodes.description: 26 variant-effect regulatory-prediction evaluations. Match-or-exceed-SOTA count out of 26.

nodes.label: SWE-bench (full)
nodes.name: SWE-bench (full)
nodes.description: Software engineering benchmark - real GitHub issues from popular Python repositories (full 2,294 task instances; Devin evaluated on 570-issue subset)

nodes.label: MultiAgentBench Research (Task Score)
nodes.name: MultiAgentBench Research (Task Score)
nodes.description: Research scenario Task Score (TS%) from MultiAgentBench/MARBLE (ACL 2025, arxiv 2503.01935). Multi-agent collaborative research task with milestone-based KPI; agents coordinate via star/chain/tree/graph topologies. Higher is better.

nodes.label: MultiAgentBench Coding (Task Score)
nodes.name: MultiAgentBench Coding (Task Score)
nodes.description: Coding scenario Task Score (TS%) from MultiAgentBench/MARBLE (ACL 2025). Multi-agent collaborative software task with role-specialized agents and milestone-graded outcomes. Higher is better.

nodes.label: MultiAgentBench Bargaining (Task Score)
nodes.name: MultiAgentBench Bargaining (Task Score)
nodes.description: Bargaining scenario Task Score (TS%) from MultiAgentBench/MARBLE (ACL 2025). Competitive multi-agent negotiation; measures task achievement under adversarial peer agents. Higher is better.

nodes.label: MultiAgentBench Minecraft (Task Score)
nodes.name: MultiAgentBench Minecraft (Task Score)
nodes.description: Minecraft cooperative-build scenario Task Score (TS%) from MultiAgentBench/MARBLE (ACL 2025). Embodied multi-agent task in Minecraft; tests planning + dynamic-environment coordination. Higher is better.

nodes.label: AgentBench Overall (OA)
nodes.name: AgentBench Overall (OA)
nodes.description: AgentBench Overall (OA) composite from THUDM AgentBench (ICLR 2024, arxiv 2308.03688). Aggregate of 8 agent environments: OS, DB, KG, DCG, LTP, HH, WS, M2W. Scale 0-5 (higher is better). First multi-environment LLM-as-Agent benchmark.

nodes.label: MetaGPT SoftwareDev Executability
nodes.name: MetaGPT SoftwareDev Executability
nodes.description: Executability score on the SoftwareDev dataset from MetaGPT (ICLR 2024, arxiv 2308.00352). 1-4 scale rating compileability/runnability of multi-agent-framework-generated software (1=fail, 4=flawless). Scaffold + backbone joint score.

nodes.label: METR 50% Time Horizon
nodes.name: METR 50% Time Horizon
nodes.description: Task duration (in minutes, by human-expert completion time) at which the model reaches 50% completion reliability on METR's 228-task suite (HCAST + RE-Bench + long-horizon). Higher = longer autonomous-work horizon. METR Time Horizon 1.1 (Jan 2026).

nodes.label: METR 80% Time Horizon
nodes.name: METR 80% Time Horizon
nodes.description: Task duration (in minutes) at which the model reaches 80% completion reliability on METR's 228-task suite. Stricter reliability threshold than p50. METR Time Horizon 1.1 (Jan 2026).

nodes.label: CoT Faithfulness (avg)
nodes.name: CoT Faithfulness (avg)
nodes.description: Rate at which a reasoning model, after silently using a hint to change its answer, explicitly verbalizes the hint in its chain-of-thought. Average across 6 hint types. Anthropic Alignment Science (Apr 2025).

nodes.label: CoT Faithfulness (misaligned hints)
nodes.name: CoT Faithfulness (misaligned hints)
nodes.description: CoT faithfulness restricted to misaligned / unauthorized-access hint types (subset of overall measure). Anthropic Apr 2025.

nodes.label: Apollo — Oversight Subversion Rate
nodes.name: Apollo — Oversight Subversion Rate
nodes.description: Fraction of trials where the model proactively disabled an oversight mechanism (cat/edit/sed of monitoring config) when given a long-term goal in conflict with developer goals. Apollo Research, Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming (Dec 2024 / arxiv:2412.04984).

nodes.label: Apollo — Deception Persistence
nodes.name: Apollo — Deception Persistence
nodes.description: Fraction of follow-up interrogation turns in which the model continued to deny scheming behavior after being directly asked. Higher = more persistent deception. Apollo Research (Dec 2024).

nodes.label: RewardBench 2 (overall)
nodes.name: RewardBench 2 (overall)
nodes.description: Allen AI multi-skill reward-model benchmark. 4-way completion choice (random=25%) across factuality, instruction-following, math, safety, focus, ties. RewardBench 2 paper (arxiv:2506.01937) / HF leaderboard.

nodes.label: ProcessBench (overall F1)
nodes.name: ProcessBench (overall F1)
nodes.description: Step-level error-detection F1 across GSM8K / MATH / OlympiadBench / OmniMath subsets (3,400 hand-annotated math reasoning traces). Qwen / ACL 2025 (arxiv:2412.06559).
